record.paper_title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
record.original_question: Determine the homology groups H_*(M,V) for equivariant map Lie algebras M and M-modules V, including the structural consequences for the abelianization H0(M,Mad) = M / [M,M] and for identifying perfect equivariant map algebras.

evidence.quote: A related problem is to determine the homology groups H∗ (M, V ). Some re- sults on H0 (M, Mad ) = M/[M, M] are contained in [NSS12] and [NS], see for example Lemmas 6.1 and 6.10 of [NS] describing classes of perfect equivariant map

algebras. The interest in perfect equivariant map algebras comes from Theorem 3.2 which indicates that these algebras have a simpler representation theory. A second reason is that perfect Lie algebras have universal central extensions, as discussed in Section 4.3.3 below.

artifact.self_contained_problem:
Let $X$ be a scheme (or algebraic variety) over an algebraically closed field $k$ of characteristic zero, and let $\mathfrak{g}$ be a finite-dimensional Lie algebra over $k$. Let $\Gamma$ be a finite group acting on both $X$ (by automorphisms of schemes) and on $\mathfrak{g}$ (by Lie algebra automorphisms). The associated equivariant map algebra is the Lie algebra of $\Gamma$-equivariant regular maps from $X$ to $\mathfrak{g}$,
$$M = M(X,\mathfrak{g})^{\Gamma} = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes_{k} \mathcal{O}(X))^{\Gamma},$$
with bracket induced from $\mathfrak{g}$ and pointwise multiplication in the coordinate ring $\mathcal{O}(X)$.

For an $M$-module $V$, the Lie algebra homology groups $H_{n}(M, V)$ ($n \ge 0$) are defined as the homology of the Chevalley–Eilenberg complex
$$\cdots \to V \otimes \Lambda^{n+1} M \to V \otimes \Lambda^{n} M \to \cdots \to V \to 0$$
with the standard differential. In particular $H_{0}(M, V) = V / M\cdot V$, and for the adjoint module $V = M_{\mathrm{ad}}$ one has $H_{0}(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$, the abelianization.

Recall that $M$ is called perfect if $[M,M] = M$, equivalently if $H_{0}(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = 0$.

Problem: Determine the Lie algebra homology groups $H_{*}(M, V)$ for equivariant map algebras $M = (\mathfrak{g} \otimes \mathcal{O}(X))^{\Gamma}$ and natural classes of $M$-modules $V$ (such as the adjoint module, the trivial module, and evaluation modules). In particular:
(a) Compute $H_{0}(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}}) = M/[M,M]$ in terms of $X$, $\mathfrak{g}$, and the $\Gamma$-action, and thereby characterize precisely those triples $(X, \mathfrak{g}, \Gamma)$ for which $M$ is perfect.
(b) Compute the higher homology groups $H_{n}(M, V)$ for $n \ge 1$, in particular $H_{1}(M, k)$ (controlling universal central extensions when $M$ is perfect) and $H_{2}(M, k)$.
artifact.status_search_result: This is posed as an open problem in a survey on equivariant map algebras. Partial results exist for $H_0(M, M_{\mathrm{ad}})$ and the characterization of perfect equivariant map algebras (e.g., in work of Neher–Savage and Neher–Savage–Senesi), but a full computation of $H_*(M, V)$ in this generality does not appear to be available in the literature, so the problem is best classified as open.

status_evidence.title: A survey of equivariant map algebras with open problems
status_evidence.snippet: A related problem is to determine the homology groups H_*(M, V). Some results on H_0(M, M_ad) = M/[M,M] are contained in references describing classes of perfect equivariant map algebras.
status_evidence.claim: Computing H_*(M,V) is listed as an open problem, with only partial results on H_0 and perfectness available.
